subject: ventures/influencer-media-kit-generator
auditor: agent session (Claude), independent quality auditor subagent, see run record
professional: a talent manager / influencer-marketing agency lead who assembles media kits and rate cards for creators; they check first which engagement-rate convention the kit states (by followers vs by reach, over what period), whether the stats carry an as-of date, whether average views/impressions are shown alongside followers, where any suggested rates come from, and whether competitor comparisons are sourced

evidence.correctness: The tool computes no numbers: followers, engagement and prices are typed text that generator.mjs parses, labels, escapes and lays out, so correctness is about faithful transformation. Probe (scratchpad/imk/probe.mjs, node probe.mjs <venture dir>) against the shipped generator.mjs: an engagement rate recomputed by the industry by-followers definition ((likes+comments)/followers x 100: (1500+264)/42000 = 4.20%) is carried verbatim as '4.2% engagement' (pass); '42% open' is left unlabelled as the docstring promises (pass); HTML escaping of '<b>' matches the OWASP five-character set (pass); validateMediaKit({}) returns the 2 errors and 4 warnings it documents (pass); prefill mergeLines appends only the new line and never duplicates (pass). Wrong outputs on plausible input: a rate row 'Bundle (Reel | 3 Stories) | $900' parses to price '3 Stories)' and the $900 is silently dropped, and a URL containing '|' is truncated, with no warning (generator.mjs:44). Playwright build of the worked example renders every section with the typed values. 3 for faithful transformation; the silent truncation keeps it from 4.
evidence.completeness: Walked in Playwright (http.server, chromium): Load example -> Build renders all seven sections (About, Reach, Audience, Past partnerships, What brands say, Rate card, Contact) in the preview with the missing-photo warning; Download yields jamie-rivers-media-kit.html (5,333 bytes, no script tags, self-contained); the plain-text one-sheet fills; the brand-deal-rate-calculator handoff banner shows the carried line and inserts it only on click; no horizontal scroll at 375 px; no console errors. Autosave, opt-out counter and prefill caps are covered by passing tests. No stubs or TODOs. Every claimed feature works; 3.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture: 60 pass, 0 fail. Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: engagementLabel regex anchor removed (generator.mjs:70) SURVIVED, because engagementLabel has no test at all; apostrophe escape removed (generator.mjs:22) caught; rate-card warning threshold 0->1 (generator.mjs:102) caught; blank-first-segment skip removed (generator.mjs:45) caught; rate price cell swapped for service (generator.mjs:197) caught. 4 of 5 caught; no test covers URL schemes or a '|' inside a value.
evidence.craft: Read generator.mjs (348 lines), prefill.mjs, index.html script, vs-kitly.html, README. Clean, pure module with consistent escaping and a careful, allowlisted, append-only handoff. Defects: every href (platform url generator.mjs:154, collab url :178, website :208, photo src :251) is HTML-escaped but its scheme is never checked, so 'javascript:' survives; the preview is an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe (index.html:185, :384), so it runs in the tool's origin. Confirmed in Playwright: a crafted link '#platformsRaw=Instagram | 1 | 1% | javascript:alert(document.domain)' shows the banner, and after Add -> Build a click on the platform link fired a dialog reading 'localhost' (the parent origin, which holds the draft in localStorage); the same href ships in the downloaded kit a brand opens. The pipe split has no escape and no warning on extra segments (generator.mjs:44). buildMediaKitHtml and buildOneSheetText re-extract the same 14 fields separately (:123-138, :289-302). 2.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty, no-SLA and privacy text present on index and both comparison pages (page.test.mjs passes); grep finds no fetch, sendBeacon or external script in index.html, usage.mjs or state.mjs, backing 'nothing sent to a server'. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origins in llms.txt/sitemap/robots/canonicals (the duncan-haywood.github.io links in source llms.txt are rewritten at deploy, source-only). Unbacked or contradicted: index.html:200 and its FAQ JSON-LD say 'no watermark, and no upsell', but every downloaded kit carries a 'Built with the free, no-signup Media Kit Generator' credit link in its footer (generator.mjs:275), visible on screen to the brand; vs-kitly.html:48-55 and :13 state Kitly's tier structure ('free tier for a single connected social account and media kit, paid tiers unlocking more connected accounts, kits and reports') 'per its own public positioning', yet no file cites a Kitly URL or check date and portfolio/ledger/2026-09.yaml:28107-28113 records that Kitly's pricing page was unreachable and the page rests on WebSearch; kitly.app returns proxy 403 here, and the only extract found (influencermarketinghub.com review, undated) is consistent with the claim. Consistent but unsourced; 2.
evidence.fitness: As a solo creator replying to 'send your media kit', the job finishes in minutes: worked example to downloaded HTML and copied text in one sitting (Playwright walk). As the named talent manager it falls short in the first hour: the Reach row has only Followers | Engagement | URL (generator.mjs:73, :153-157), so no average views, reach or impressions, which brands ask for first on TikTok/YouTube/Reels; the only date in the kit is the footer 'generated' line, which @media print hides (generator.mjs:245), so a printed/PDF kit carries no as-of date for its stats; one kit at a time with no roster; rate card has no usage-rights/whitelisting/exclusivity line items beyond a footnote. Not tied to any ranked paid bet in portfolio/monetization/bets.md. 2.
evidence.domain: Against common influencer-marketing practice (engagement rate by followers = (likes+comments[+saves+shares])/followers; by reach = interactions/reach, typically quoted over the last 10-30 posts or 30-90 days; brand intake forms ask for average views and impressions and a stats date): the tool states no convention and offers no field for it, appending ' engagement' to a bare number (generator.mjs:67-71) so '4.2%' by reach and '4.2%' by followers, which differ several-fold, read identically; a fraction typed as '0.042' becomes '0.042 engagement'. It suggests no rates itself (example $450/$150/$600 are placeholders, and rates are delegated to the sibling brand-deal-rate-calculator), which is the honest choice. The rate-card note on usage rights, exclusivity and turnaround matches practice. A talent manager would sign off the layout and content list, not the reach section as a brand-facing standard. 2.

defects.what: href/src values are escaped but their scheme is never checked, so a javascript: URL (typed, or carried in by a crafted handoff link) ships in the downloaded kit and, because the preview is an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe, executes in the tool's own origin on click (Playwright: dialog 'localhost')
a '|' inside a service name or URL silently splits the row: 'Bundle (Reel | 3 Stories) | $900' shows price '3 Stories)' and drops $900, with no warning
the kit's only date is the footer 'generated' line, hidden by @media print, so a printed/PDF kit carries no as-of date for its follower and engagement stats
no engagement-rate convention (by followers vs by reach, period) and no average views/reach/impressions column; a bare number is labelled ' engagement' whatever it measures
'no watermark, and no upsell' while every downloaded kit carries a 'Built with the free, no-signup Media Kit Generator' credit link visible to the brand
Kitly tier claims attributed to 'its own public positioning' with no source URL or check date in any file; the ledger records the vendor page was unreachable when written
engagementLabel has no test; removing its end anchor (so '42% open' becomes '42% open engagement') leaves all 60 tests green

verdict: A small, clean, honest generator that does what it says: the worked example builds all seven sections, downloads a self-contained file and a plain-text copy, and the handoff from the rate calculator is careful and append-only; 60 tests pass and 4 of 5 seeded mutants are caught. It computes nothing, so its numbers are only as right as what is typed, and it suggests no rates of its own. It does not meet the bar on claims (a 'no watermark' line beside a tool credit on every kit, and unsourced Kitly tier claims) and falls short for a talent manager on domain and fitness: no stated engagement convention, no views/impressions, and no as-of date in a printed kit. The most important fix is the unchecked URL scheme, which lets a crafted handoff link put a working javascript: link into the preview and into the file a brand opens.
